:::{#def-channel-code}
#### Channel code and rate

An $(M, n)$ **channel code** for a [discrete memoryless channel](#def-channel)
sends one of $M$ messages, $w \in \{1, \dots, M\}$, in $n$ uses of the channel.
It has

- an *encoder*, which maps each message $w$ to a *codeword*
  $(x_1(w), \dots, x_n(w))$ of $n$ inputs, and
- a *decoder*, which maps each sequence of $n$ outputs to a guess at $w$.

Its **rate** is

$$R \eqdef \frac{\log_2 M}{n} \text{ bits per channel use},$$

and its **maximal probability of error** $\lambda^{(n)}$
is the largest, over messages $w$,
of the probability that the decoder's guess is wrong when $w$ is sent.
These are the definitions of @cover2006elements [section 7.5].

:::
